headline: Lightning’s Victor Herman out day-to-day with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Lightning player Victor Herman is out day-to-day with a lower-body injury. The outlet's summary notes only that Hedman has two goals and four points through 10 games with Tampa Bay this season, and it doesn't say how long Herman might be out or which lineup spot he fills.

The team around him is in good shape so far this season. TBL is 7-3-0 for 14 points, and its share of expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates, as a percentage) sits at 57.1%, or 58% at five-on-five. That says the Lightning are winning the shot-quality battle, not just collecting results. The caveat is finishing and goaltending: they are 2.8 goals below expected and 1.4 goals saved below expected, so the record has come despite some bad puck luck. If that evens out, the standings should look even better. The special teams are solid too, at 0.66 expected goals per game on the power play and 0.56 allowed per game on the penalty kill. We have no data on Herman himself or on who would take his minutes, so we'd wait for a clearer timeline before drawing conclusions about the lineup.
